hook_text: Draw lines around an orange and you can find any place on Earth. How?
clip_script: Polokwane, Grade 6, a bag of oranges. Draw a line around the middle: the equator, zero degrees latitude. Draw more rings above and below: lines of latitude, up to ninety degrees at the poles. Now draw lines from top to bottom: lines of longitude, measured east and west of the Greenwich Meridian, up to one hundred and eighty degrees. The Tropic of Capricorn crosses Limpopo, just north of Polokwane. Rings and segments: a grid for the whole Earth.
visual_style: Whiteboard orange turning into a globe as rings of latitude and pole-to-pole lines of longitude draw themselves.
mood: Hands-on and surprising, like a science trick that really works.
pacing: Slow first line around the middle, then quicker rings and segments, ending on the full grid.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw your own latitude and longitude lines on a ball or fruit.
